pooled_hartung_knapp.why_it_is_shown: Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.5 recommends Hartung-Knapp where k is small. Shown ALONGSIDE the unadjusted interval, not instead of it. A FLOOR OF 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never NARROW the interval below the unadjusted one.

heterogeneity.DIRECTION_TEST: NOT APPLICABLE -- I-squared is 0.0%, below the threshold at which the direction test is informative. The trials are consistent with a common effect and no heterogeneity caution is warranted. Applying one here would manufacture doubt the data do not support, which is the mirror failure of ignoring heterogeneity that matters.
heterogeneity.how_to_read_this_at_low_k: At k=2 or k=3 these statistics are weak evidence about consistency in EITHER direction. A low value means the estimates are CONSISTENT WITH a common effect, not that one is demonstrated.
heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: UNDECIDABLE from this object. I-squared is 0 and Q is below the degrees of freedom, where the Higgins form is negative-and-clamped and the REML/metafor form is exactly zero -- BOTH DEFINITIONS GIVE 0 and nothing here distinguishes them. Recorded as undecidable rather than guessed.

per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2). The RR formula is Cochrane Handbook v6.5 section 6.4.1, Box 6.4.a. The standard error formula is NOT in the Handbook -- chapter 6 defers it to the RevMan statistical algorithms (Statistical algorithms and calculations used in Review Manager), and that is its source here. Checked against the live Handbook on 2026-08-26. Counts read from the registry; only the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown.
per_trial.registered_eligibility: Key Inclusion Criteria: 1. Healthy infants born between 29 weeks 0 days and 34 weeks 6 days GA. 2. Infants who are entering their first full RSV season at the time of screening. Key Exclusion Criteria: 1. Meets American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) or other local criteria to receive commercial palivizumab. 2. Any fever (\>= 100.4°F \[\>= 38.0°C\], regardless of route) or lower respiratory illness within 7 days prior to randomization. 3. Acute illness (defined as the presence of moderate or severe signs and symptoms) at the time of randomization. 4. Active RSV infection (a child with signs/symptoms of respiratory infection must have negative RSV testing) or known prior history of RSV infection. 5. Receipt of palivizumab or other RSV monoclonal antibody or any RSV vaccine, including maternal RSV vaccination.

primary.outcome: medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection
primary.the_third_trial_EXCLUDED_and_why: NCT05437510 (HARMONIE) IS SEEDED ON THIS PAGE AND IS NOT IN THIS POOL. Its comparator arm is typed NO_INTERVENTION and titled 'No preventive intervention' -- an OPEN-LABEL UNTREATED control, not a placebo. The two pooled trials are PLACEBO_COMPARATOR and double-blind. An untreated open-label control cannot be pooled with a blinded placebo control on a MEDICALLY ATTENDED endpoint, because whether a carer seeks medical attention is exactly the kind of outcome unblinding moves. Its counts are recorded so the exclusion is checkable: nirsevimab 11/4038 against no intervention 64/4019.

published_synthesis_comparison.what_is_owed: No published synthesis or regulatory review of the nirsevimab programme has been read.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that either trial is free of bias -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED. NOT anything about the excluded open-label trial, which reports a large effect on its own terms and is excluded on COMPARATOR TYPE, not on quality. NOT RSV hospitalisation or mortality, neither of which is the pooled endpoint. NOT reliability at k=2 -- see Hartung-Knapp.

handbook_authority.handbook: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions
handbook_authority.c62: 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.2605 and the house-rule point is 0.2606. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: The house rule is REML with Hartung-Knapp below k=10, settled days ago. Whether it means ALWAYS or WITH A FLOOR AT k=3 is a decision about this corpus, not a computation, and it has been referred rather than taken. BOTH INTERVALS STAND ON THIS PAGE UNTIL IT IS MADE. Nothing is unpublished and no reader is left with only the narrower one.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

r_output._what_this_is: Console output of the fit as printed. NOT re-typed and NOT summarised.
r_output.call: rma(yi = yi, sei = sei, method = "REML") and the same fit with test="knha"
r_output.inputs_derivation: yi = log(point); sei = (log(ci_high) - log(ci_low)) / (2 * 1.959964), read from this object's own per_trial rows.
r_output.what_k_equals_2_means: Two trials cannot inform a between-study variance; tau^2 is estimated with ONE degree of freedom. tau^2 is exactly 0 here and Q is 0.0879 on 1 df (p = 0.7668) -- the two trials agree closely -- but AT k = 2 THAT IS CONSISTENT WITH AGREEMENT, NOT EVIDENCE OF IT.
r_output.interval_method: REML with the unadjusted Wald interval, and the same fit under Hartung-Knapp beside it. THE HOUSE INTERVAL FLOORS THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR AT max(1, SE_knha/SE_unadjusted); metafor's raw unfloored value is printed separately and flagged where it is narrower than the unadjusted interval.
r_output.why_this_was_re_run: THE PREVIOUS STORED OUTPUT LABELLED metafor's RAW knha INTERVAL 'Hartung-Knapp' with no qualifier. POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_a_published_review_pools_six_trials_wh: A PUBLISHED SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF THIS AGENT INCLUDED SIX RANDOMISED TRIALS (n = 12,086) WHERE THIS POOL CARRIES TWO. Lien et al., Pediatrics and Neonatology 2026, PMID 41314935, reports RSV-related hospitalisation at OR 0.19 (0.13 to 0.30) and severe RSV infection at OR 0.23 (0.12 to 0.44). Those are different outcomes on a different scale from this pool's medically attended RSV LRTI risk ratio of 0.2605 (0.1766 to 0.3845), so NO DISCREPANCY IS CLAIMED -- the point is the trial count.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_which_four_are_missing_is_not_establis: The review's abstract names none of its six trials and no included-study table was read, so the four trials this object does not carry are COUNTED AND NOT IDENTIFIED. Naming them would require reading the review.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_a_published_synthesis_carried_more_tri: A PUBLISHED SYNTHESIS OF THIS QUESTION INCLUDED 6 TRIALS WHERE THIS POOL CARRIES 2. Source: Lien et al., Pediatrics and Neonatology 2026, PMID 41314935, six randomised trials totalling 12,086 participants.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_whether_the_extra_trials_can_be_named: WHICH TRIALS ARE ABSENT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The published abstract names none of its included studies and no included-study table was read, so this is A DIFFERENCE IN STATED COUNTS AND NOTHING MORE. It is NOT a claim that 4 specific trials were missed, and nobody here has identified them.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_what_this_means_for_the_estimate_above: The estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. resolved_2026_08_21.the_text_that_decides_it: RoB 2 guidance 2019, Box 4, signalling question 1.1: "Answer 'No information' if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized." And section 4.4: "A judgement of low risk of bias requires that the trial has an adequate method of concealing the allocation sequence from those involved in enrolling participants, and there are no concerns about generation of the allocation sequence." Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 8.3 names the domain's three components.
resolved_2026_08_21.why_this_is_not_an_adjudicated_dispute: A blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. THAT WOULD ORDINARILY BE A DISPUTE TO ADJUDICATE. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_the_registry_gives_and_does_not: A ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: RANDOMIZED`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
resolved_2026_08_21.how_this_maps_to_the_tool_s_algorithm: The tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a DOMAIN judgement of SOME CONCERNS. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the OVERALL at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_does_not_change: NO OVERALL RATING AND NO GRADE CERTAINTY MOVES. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_would_close_it_properly: The trial publications or protocols, which carry sequence generation and concealment. Neither was read. Until one is, LOW is not available on this domain for any result in this corpus.

rob2_algorithm_2026_08_26.authority: RoB 2, Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials, Higgins/Savovic/Page/Sterne (eds), RoB2 Development Group, 22 August 2019
rob2_algorithm_2026_08_26.basis: B: the object declares a domain unjudgeable from the sources read to be NO_INFORMATION, so every signalling response is "No information" by its own declaration
rob2_algorithm_2026_08_26.this_does_not_replace_the_stored_judgeme: This is the judgement the published algorithm proposes from the signalling responses named here. grade.approach: GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.
grade.not_rated_up: No domain is rated UP. Rating up applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials starting HIGH.

steps.reason: Both results are SOME_CONCERNS, and the driver is NOT an observed weakness -- D1, D4 and D5 are LOW on read registrations, with quadruple masking including the outcomes assessor. D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION because the registry does not carry those fields, and an unjudgeable domain caps the overall.

The stored refit gives tau^2 EXACTLY ZERO, Q 0.0879 on 1 df, p = 0.7668; the two intervals -- 0.2715 (0.1689 to 0.4363) and 0.2395 (0.1214 to 0.4727) -- overlap almost entirely and agree in conclusion.

One registered primary on each trial, the same endpoint, placebo-controlled, and it is exactly what is pooled. RECORDED AND NOT USED TO DOWNGRADE: the two trials enrol different infant populations and NCT02878330 fixes a 50 mg dose where MELODY uses weight-banded dosing -- read from the registered arm labels. The endpoint definition is unaffected.

The effect is large and the interval excludes no difference by a wide margin: 0.2605 (0.1766 to 0.3845). Even the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2, 0.2606 (0.1233 to 0.5505) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df, EXCLUDES 1 across its whole range. Downgrading for imprecision here would be mechanical rather than warranted.
k = 2. Funnel-plot asymmetry tests have essentially no power below about ten trials (Handbook 13.3.5.4), so this is NOT ASSESSABLE rather than 'undetected'.

primary.summary: MODERATE certainty. The single downgrade is for two unjudgeable risk-of-bias domains that the registry does not carry -- not for inconsistency, indirectness or imprecision, none of which the evidence supports downgrading.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In Nirsevimab versus placebo for medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection in infants, what is the effect of nirsevimab versus placebo on medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against placebo.

The outcome pooled is medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection.

Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Counts and denominators read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

introduction__derived_from.reconstruction_basis: The script's own source: it builds `question` as 'In <title>, what is the effect on <tail>?' and rewrites `manuscript.introduction` to open 'This review asks: <question>' in the same pass. Both rules are read from the committed script, not inferred from the values.
introduction__derived_from.and_therefore: This introduction is NOT an independent statement of the review's question. It restates `question`, which restates `title`. Treating the two as agreeing witnesses is one fact counted twice.

question_prose_repaired_2026_08_30.introduced_by: scripts/repair_paper_reads_terribly_2026_08_24.py, which built the question as 'In <title>, what is the effect on <tail>?' where the tail already began with 'versus'.
question_prose_repaired_2026_08_30.WHAT_WAS_NOT_DONE: ⛔ NO POPULATION WAS ADDED. This question still states no population, and that is why the indirectness domain REFUSES to rate this outcome rather than deriving a rating from it. The population exists on this object in one place only -- the eligibility of the contributing trials -- and reading it off them would be inferring the question from the studies that answer it, which returns DIRECT by construction. An authored question is required and is an editorial decision, not a repair.

question__derived_from.reconstruction_basis: The script's own source: it builds `question` as 'In <title>, what is the effect on <tail>?' and rewrites `manuscript.introduction` to open 'This review asks: <question>' in the same pass. Both rules are read from the committed script, not inferred from the values.
